extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of Renaissance/medieval art history
extracted.subtask_short: assessing Renaissance fresco and panel painting
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and qualities for evaluating/producing medieval-to-Renaissance frescoes and panel paintings (composition, draughtsmanship, colour, narrative invention, technique, and artist comportment), illustrated by biographies of Buonamico, Ambrogio Lorenzetti, Pietro Cavallini, and Simone Memmi/Martini.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention / originality of composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Showed beautiful and great invention in grouping and placing his figures thoughtfully in historical scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised when a master devises new methods of composing narrative scenes (e.g., Ambrogio's treatment of a youth becoming a friar and the subsequent martyrdom with a terrible tempest). Novel ways of arranging figures that were 'unknown before' earn 'infinite commendation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping and placement of figures (composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to group and place figures gracefully and thoughtfully so that scenes read coherently and with aesthetic balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Ambrogio's careful grouping in historical scenes; Simone's use of figures and horses with admirable judgment. Positive signs include natural interactions between figures, varied poses, and avoidance of awkward crowding; negative patterns include arbitrary ornamental borders that interrupt narrative flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depiction of movement, atmosphere, and air
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterfeiting the travailing of the figures and the turmoil of the air, rain, wind, and other atmospheric effects to convey motion and weather.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambrogio's rendering of storm and wind is held up as a model from which modern masters learned. Look for convincingly worked drapery, motion in limbs and garments, and atmospheric perspective that makes motion believable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of colour and handling of medium
rubrics_metrics.description: Being a practised colourist in fresco and handling colours in distemper with dexterity and facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise is given for fresh, vivacious colouring and skilful use of the chosen medium (fresco, distemper, mosaic). Examples: Pietro Cavallini's fresh colouring and Ambrogio's panels in distemper. Consider technical appropriateness of pigments and paints for the support and subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draughtsmanship / drawing skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of drawing, line, and preparatory design — the evident worth in draughtsmanship as seen in drawings and panel predellas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambrogio's draughtsmanship is cited as demonstrable in drawings; conversely Simone is said to be 'not very excellent in draughtsmanship' though inventive. Assess clarity of outlines, correct proportions, and expressive draftsmanship in figures and faces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative organisation and scene sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to organise multiple scenes and episodes (e.g., stories on walls) so they form a coherent narrative without awkward divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised when artists 'did not divide scene from scene with ornamental borders' and instead arranged sequential episodes on slopes or within continuous space (Simone's Chapter-house work). Anti-pattern: repeatedly putting ground over sky or breaking continuity with decorative borders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifelike portraiture and likeness from life
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill in drawing portraits 'from the life' and capturing likenesses of contemporary figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simone's and Pietro's portraits (Pope Urban V, Petrarca, Madonna Laura) are noted as important achievements. Criteria include believable facial types, resemblance to sitters, and individual characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive gesture and emotional detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Rendering of gestures, facial expressions, and small actions to convey emotion and activity (e.g., musicians' varied gestures, angels' bitter weeping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for vivid, varied gestures and physiognomy that communicate the subject (Simone's musicians turn ears, open mouths, swell throats). Strong emotional detail adds vivacity and narrative clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of complex subjects (horses, crowds, battle scenes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to depict complex groups, equine anatomy, and dynamic crowd episodes with invention and judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simone is praised for horses and soldiers in beautiful attitudes; good work shows plausible movement, foreshortening, and variety of poses. Poorly rendered groups appear flat, repetitive, or anatomically incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of preparatory methods and working technique (cartoon method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of cartoons/outlines and methodical preparation to transfer designs to plaster for speed and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Old masters outlined whole works in red over plaster as a cartoon, then enlarged from small designs for rapid fresco work. This method is presented as a practical, traditional technique for large-scale frescoes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution speed and fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity to execute works quickly and with fluency without sacrificing overall effect (e.g., 'executed in so short a time', 'appears all made in one day').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised when speed coincides with technical control (junctions of plaster contrived so work appears made in one day). However, haste that yields sloppiness is implicitly criticized; balance of rapidity and quality is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical finish: junctions, seams, and fresco integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of technical finish such as junctions of plaster, making the fresco read as unified and fresh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pietro's work is noted for junctions so well contrived that the piece 'appears all made in one day.' Assessors should note seamless joins, consistent surface texture, and durable application to plaster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of materials and their restorability
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of materials (e.g., water-colours without size, distemper) and consequences for appearance and restoration (a wet sponge sufficed to remove an alteration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Buonamico's anecdote — painting a child as a little bear in water colours without size, later removable with a wet sponge — illustrates how material choices affect permanence and the possibility of restoration or alteration. Consider permanence and intended longevity when judging material choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and synthesis of stylistic sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to blend different manners (e.g., Greek manner with Giotto) or adopt useful principles from masters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pietro blended Greek manner and Giotto's style; such synthesis is praised when it produces superior effects. Evaluate whether borrowing advances invention or results in incoherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architectural accuracy and depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Faithful depiction of architectural forms and use of models/designs (e.g., painting the Church as drawn from Arnolfo's model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simone's painted rendering of S. Maria del Fiore from the architect's model is valued as a record; good work shows accurate perspective, believable built space, and respectful use of architectural sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist's moral comportment and learnedness
rubrics_metrics.description: The artist's manners, letters, modesty, and conduct are regarded as accompaniment to their art and affect their reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambrogio is praised for 'ways of a gentleman and philosopher' and for attention to letters in youth; the text presents courteous ways and modesty as honourable accompaniments. While not a pictorial criterion, historical reception often weighs an artist's character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious devotion and piety as reception factors
rubrics_metrics.description: An artist's piety, charity, and devout life inform contemporary esteem and sometimes the interpretation of their works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pietro and others are described as devout and friends of the poor; such qualities contribute to their reputation and the miracles or reverence associated with certain works. This is evaluation of the artist's social-religious standing rather than purely technical merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability and preservation (condition affects judgment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The survival, preservation, and later treatment (whitewashing, damp, renovation) of works influence how they are judged and what can be seen of the master's skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple examples: paintings eaten away by time, whitewashed frescoes, or works ruined by later interventions. Critics should note that technical and aesthetic assessment can be limited by condition and later alterations.
